# Native formats: Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, HTML and R

Read this when the chart has to live somewhere other than a PNG: a native, editable chart in a deck or workbook, a Power BI report, a web page or R. The workflow in `SKILL.md` (question, chart type, headline, QA) still applies; this page covers the build for each platform. Each cookbook page has a section per platform with the steps for that chart.

- **HTML:** the chart-card pattern with `assets/web/mck-viz.css` plus `assets/web/mck-plotly-template.js` or `assets/web/vega-lite-config.json` (starter: `assets/html/chart-card.html`).
- **Excel / PowerPoint:** build a **native, editable chart**, never a pasted picture, when a pptx tool is available. With Python and python-pptx, a ranking is one call: `mckviz.office.bar_slide` on `mckviz.office.deck()`, then `mckviz.office.save` (the cookbook's bar page shows it). In Claude.ai, or any environment with a pptx skill (pptxgenjs), use it with the theme and chart options in `assets/office/pptxgenjs-theme.js` (`MCK.theme`, `MCK.text.*` on the slide grid, `MCK.barChart` with `MCK.pointColors(labels, focus)`) and the recipe in `references/office-setup.md` ("A native chart from code with pptxgenjs"): the headline in the title placeholder at 26 pt Bold McKesson Blue, the subtitle and source as text, and the benchmark line and bold focus labels as shapes over the pinned plot area. Without a pptx tool, start from the starter deck (`McKesson-DataViz-Starter.pptx`, native charts on the template grid) and follow the cookbook page's Excel / PowerPoint section by hand, or render a PNG with matplotlib and place it on the slide as the last resort.
- **Power BI, R:** follow the cookbook page's section for that platform, using the theme files in `assets/` (Office files: see Setup below).
